title: AWS SDK for .NET, CI/CD, shared responsibility
exp: As a .NET developer joining a data engineering team, you bridge the .NET API layer with the AWS data pipeline.
pts: AWSSDK.S3 NuGet package: AmazonS3Client reads credentials from env vars -> ~/.aws/credentials -> EC2 instance profile.
Never hardcode access keys. Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance for automatic temporary credentials.
Shared responsibility: AWS secures hardware/network. YOU secure IAM, encryption, network config.
CI/CD: GitHub Actions with OIDC (no long-lived keys stored) is the modern standard.

viz.note: Credential chain: EC2 code -> SDK checks env vars -> checks ~/.aws/credentials -> checks instance metadata (IAM role) -> temporary credentials returned.

qa.q: How should a .NET app on EC2 access S3 without hardcoded credentials?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Attach an IAM Role (instance profile) to the EC2 instance. The AWS SDK automatically reads temporary credentials from the EC2 metadata service -- no access keys in code. Credentials auto-rotate every hour. Same pattern applies to Lambda (execution role), ECS (task role), and EMR (cluster role).

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** C# compiler synthesizes an IAsyncStateMachine struct. Awaiting incomplete tasks yields control to the caller; thread pool threads resume via TaskScheduler/SynchronizationContext.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Blocking async code with .Result or .Wait() on single-threaded synchronization contexts leads to deadlocks and thread pool starvation.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Async preserves thread pool scalability for I/O operations, but introduces state machine allocations and complex exception bubbling.

interviewPlaybook.openingScript: In enterprise cloud environments, AWS SDK for .NET, CI/CD, shared responsibility must be designed with fault tolerance, zero-downtime deployment pipelines, and explicit security boundaries.
interviewPlaybook.incidentStory: A regional outage threatened pipeline ingestion availability when a dependency failed around AWS SDK for .NET, CI/CD, shared responsibility. Using infrastructure-as-code and automated failover, I implemented circuit breaking and fallback routing, keeping client payload ingestion at 99.99% availability.
